chapter: Bass, drums and the big-band rhythm section
title: Drummer's job, Curly Russell, and New Orleans drum styles
summary: On 52nd Street drummers stopped carrying the beat; Ramey recalls Walter Page's lessons and New Orleans versus Chicago drumming.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: And I don't care how fast the tempo was, or how difficult it was or how ragged it got, they had to have a strong bass player to carry that beat while the drummer, instead of carryin' the tempo, he was decoratin' and actually, stealin' the solo from the horns in places. But it became such an exciting thing that they accepted it, you know. But now this was created by the Basie rhythm section, by the man that I adore most, 'cause he actually made that Basie a rhythm section. Continuously, when they were first playing, when Jo Jones first came, he used to call Jo Jones 'Baby' to tell them to remember that that drum is not supposed to sound any louder than that piano over there or that guitar, unamplified.
That's what he used to tell 'em.

He said, "Now, come on down." He said, "See if you do all that stuff, and come on down." Now, if you think back, during the time of "King" Oliver and those days, that drummer swung the band. I don't care who you had. They had to have a bass

horn because a bass fiddle could not compete with it, y'know. And there was a one-man rhythm section. That drummer, all you could hear was pop-wop-wop-wop--you know, that bass drum. And I call that the New Orleans style. Then it goes on to Chicago style, where the drummer not only used his foot, but he did play some on the cymbals.
If you notice, the New Orleans drummer used to play it on his snare drum, mostly.
If you see Baby Lovett he's a good example of that. He still is a genius on those snares.
Where did Baby Lovett come from?
He is from New Orleans? Oh, I see.
Yeah. That's the way they were taught. You can swing a man with those snare drums, although he doesn't play that big foot--heavy foot like the--
Zutty ? If you remember, he plays the snare and the rims, you know, and then in later years he started playin' the cymbals. But now, in Chicago, then, you notice that they began to play the cymbals.
